title: EID MAR denarius of Brutus
description: Silver denarius minted by Brutus's forces in the East. Obverse: bare head of Brutus with BRVT IMP L PLAET CEST. Reverse: pileus (liberty cap) between two daggers, with EID MAR below. The most explicit numismatic commemoration of Caesar's assassination.
location: British Museum (example: BM 1919,1119.1); other collections worldwide. Approximately 80 specimens known.

title: Marble portrait bust identified as Brutus (Museo Nazionale Romano)
description: Marble portrait head in the Museo Nazionale Romano (Palazzo Massimo, Inv. 595). Identified as Brutus through facial comparison with the EID MAR denarius portrait and other numismatic evidence. Features a lean face, receding hairline, and intense expression consistent with coin portraits.
location: Museo Nazionale Romano, Palazzo Massimo alle Terme, Rome, Inv. 595.
note: needs_verification: confirm inventory number and identification through published scholarship. The identification has scholarly support but is not universally accepted.

title: Later imagined portraits of Brutus (Renaissance to modern)
description: Post-classical paintings and sculptures imagining Brutus, particularly in the Renaissance and Neoclassical periods. Examples include the Capitoline 'Brutus' bronze (actually a 4th-3rd century BCE Etruscan or Roman work misidentified as L. Junius Brutus) and 18th-19th century Neoclassical paintings of Brutus sentencing his sons or reading after the assassination. These are later art, not contemporary likenesses.
note: These are reception artifacts, not historical evidence. They reflect post-classical political and artistic engagement with Brutus's story, not his actual appearance.
